commercially Sodium metal is obtained from the electrolysis of molten
Sodium Chloride (NaCl) inthe Down Cell.
Construction of the Down Cell
The down cell consists of steel container lined inside with firebricks. The
anode is made of Graphite at the center which emerges from the bottom,
above which there is dome for the collection of Chlorine gas- The cathode is
circular and made of Copper or Iron. The cathode and anode are separated
by an iron screen, so that the two products of electrolysis, namely Sodium
and Chlorine gas are kept apart and are collected separately. The molten
Sodium collects in the cathode compartment where it rises to the top and is
taped off via a pipe. On the other hand, gaseous Chlorine, as by-product is
collected, at anode andis collected from the other pipe.
